title: Usage export subscription: schema versioning, filtered delta delivery, and owner S3 prefixes
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Problem: Customers want long-running export subscriptions that deliver only the records they care about (per-tenant filters and event types) and that can safely evolve over time without breaking downstream consumers. Current ad-hoc and scheduled exports are batch-oriented and tightly coupled to a single CSV schema.

Goal: Implement subscription-based usage exports that support: (1) schema versioning with clear migration paths, (2) filtered delta delivery (per-subscription predicates and time-window deltas), (3) customer-controlled S3 prefix targets and retention metadata, and (4) webhook fallback for low-latency subscribers.

Scope & approach:
- Add a subscription metadata record in the exports service describing filter, preferred delivery mode (S3 CSV full/delta, S3 Parquet, webhook), desired CSV schema version (or AUTO), and target S3 prefix/role.
- Export pipeline will produce compact delta files using a stable header linked to a schema version id. Each file carries a small manifest (metadata header row) with schema_id, export_window_start/end, record_count, checksum, and signing token.
- Implement server-side schema registry for export CSV schemas (schema_id -> column list + typed hints). Provide migration tooling to emit both old/new column sets for N releases during rollouts.
- Filtering: evaluate predicate at serialization time; for delta exports the pipeline will compute changed-sets via time-window delta on normalized usage records (not raw event rows) to avoid duplicate semantics.
- Delivery: S3 target will support customer-managed prefixes and cross-account role assumption (we create presigned write helpers and optionally assumeRole for putObject). Webhook fallback will send a single manifest + URL list and optionally a small payload sample.
- Backfills & compatibility: when a schema upgrade occurs for a subscription, emit sidecar compatibility CSVs for 2 export cycles; provide a console migration preview and a CLI diff tool.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Customers can create a subscription with filter and delivery preference via Console/CLI/API.
2) Pipeline emits per-subscription delta CSVs with schema_id in header and uploads to requested S3 prefix using configured credentials.
3) Schema registry supports adding a non-breaking column and a planned breaking change flow requiring explicit opt-in.
4) Webhook fallback can be enabled; in case of S3 write failures we retry and then invoke webhook with error manifest.
5) We have an automated migration runbook and integration tests covering header validation, checksum, and role-assume flows.

Rollout plan: feature flag gated; pilot with 3 customers (internal + 2 early adopters) for 4 weeks. Monitor failure rate, end-to-end latency, S3 write permissions errors, and schema mismatch alerts in Console.

Docs & artifacts: design doc (confluence) link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/EXPORTS-SUBSCRIPTION-SCHEMA, PR template: github.com/redwood-inference/exports/pull/---, integration tests: github.com/redwood-inference/exports/tree/eng-24680/tests
